implement.summary:
Defect on BASE_SHA (VERIFIED): supabase/functions/api/index.ts:1984-2009 `readAllRows` paged owner inventories by OFFSET (`.range(from,to)`) and stopped after `MAX_PAGES = 20` full pages, returning `{ rows }` as if complete — so GET /v1/progress (buildProgress, index.ts:2651-2668, tables progress_daily and practice_days) silently served 20_000 of 21_003 rows as the owner's whole history (200, wrong streak), and a source that kept repeating a page was also answered 200. The only 'incomplete' outcome that existed was a page error; truncation and stalls were indistinguishable from completion. accountDeletionOperations.ts had no inventory reader at all.

Fix: accountDeletionOperations.ts gains a general owner-inventory reader — `readOwnerInventory(reader)` walks a keyset cursor (`readPage(cursor, limit)` / `cursorAfter(row)` / `cursorKey`) with no page cap and returns a discriminated `InventoryReadResult`: `{status:'COMPLETE', rows, pages}` only when the end is proven (a page shorter than `limit`, or an empty page after exact multiples of the page size), otherwise `{status:'INCOMPLETE', reason:'page_error'|'cursor_stalled'|'page_overflow', error, httpStatus, rows, pages}` (source error, a cursor that does not advance, or a page larger than requested). `completedInventoryRows(result)` is the consumer helper: rows for COMPLETE, `null` for INCOMPLETE, so deletion/cleanup code cannot mistake a partial inventory for done. `postgrestKeysetBefore([{column,value}…])` builds the PostgREST `or=(…)` row-value predicate for a DESCENDING composite key with column-name validation and quote/backslash escaping; `INVENTORY_PAGE_ROWS = 1000` matches hosted PostgREST max_rows.

Wiring (shipping path): index.ts `readAllRows` now delegates to `readOwnerInventory` — pages are `.or(<keyset before>).order(...).limit(1000)` with no offset; the composite keys are (day, shot_type, scoring_model_version) for progress_daily and (day) for practice_days. COMPLETE → `{ rows }` as before; any INCOMPLETE → `{ error }` → the existing `serviceUnavailable('Progress', …)` 503, never a 200 with a truncated history.

Regression test (committed first, 3617549b/5e3b1bf2, then adjusted in 01de13be): __wf__/inventory_pagination.test.ts — reader unit tests (17_003 & 21_003 rows complete with no cap, exact multiples need the empty proof page, stall/page-error/overflow are INCOMPLETE, consumer helper returns null for INCOMPLETE, keyset predicate escaping/validation) plus route tests through the real Edge handler with a PostgREST-like stand-in that parses `or=(…)`, `order`, `limit`: 21 pages of practice_days and 21 exact pages of progress_daily are all served (limit=1000, no offset, cursor predicate on every page after the first), a stalled source → 503, a mid-stream page error → 503. On BASE it fails 11/12 (20000 vs 21003, 20000 vs 21000, 200 vs 503); on HEAD 12/12 pass.

implement.approach: Generic cursor reader `readOwnerInventory(reader)` in accountDeletionOperations.ts: pages by keyset (`readPage(cursor, limit)` → `cursorAfter(row)`), CONTINUES after every non-empty page (short or full) and treats ONLY an empty page as proof of completion (closes the r1 P1: PostgREST db-max-rows clamps answer 200 with a short page). Any anomaly returns `{status:'INCOMPLETE', reason, rows(diagnostic), pages, error, httpStatus}`: page_error (PostgREST error or thrown reader), malformed_page (null/non-array data without error), page_overflow (more rows than requested), repeated_row (cursor key seen before → stalled/overlapping/ignored cursor), invalid_page_size, page_budget (INVENTORY_MAX_PAGES=1000 × 1000 rows). `completedInventoryRows(result)` returns rows only for COMPLETE (null otherwise) so deletion/cleanup consumers cannot mistake a partial inventory for done. `postgrestKeysetBefore`/`postgrestKeysetAfter` build the descending-order PostgREST `or=(and(a.eq,b.eq,c.lt),and(a.eq,b.lt),a.lt)` filter from the ordered unique columns, with column-name validation and quote/backslash escaping. index.ts `readAllRows` (buildProgress: progress_daily keyed by day,shot_type,scoring_model_version; practice_days keyed by day) uses `.or(before).order(...).limit(limit)` instead of `.range()`+MAX_PAGES and maps INCOMPLETE to the existing generic 503 via `serviceUnavailable('Progress', failureDetail(...))`; non-page-error reasons log as `{name:'UnexpectedResult', code: INV01..INV05}` (INVENTORY_INCOMPLETE_CODES), no new console sink, body unchanged.
